ask.question: A UE5.8 project runs one shared checkout with 16 git worktrees and multiple agents; the working tree was clobbered twice today, a foreign staged case-rename was swept into a commit, and Perforce holds 1,294 pending opens (CL 307: 745 mixed files incl. 458 HoudiniEngine temp cooks; CL 303: 543 files from the interiors lane; 2 single-file CLs). Tonight we created p4 checkpoint.48, p4d logon persistence, pruned LFS, and pushed the lane branch. Which single source-control structural fix has the highest value next? Answer with the option letter only.

result.reason: Retiring stale worktrees and enforcing one worktree per lane removes the shared-checkout collision surface behind repeated clobbering, while one-off backlog cleanup does not prevent recurrence.
